scope: Read-only design review; no remote or source edits
question: Does changing the time term weight alone alter the fixed Cap MLP16 Validation tradeoff?

recommended_design.evaluation: Validation only; full Validation raw RMSE first strict finite minimum checkpoint

alternatives.limitation: Tests only reduced time weighting despite opposite observed median imbalance across datasets.

alternatives.design: Same alpha=.1/10 on all datasets, eighteen new fits
alternatives.cost: Twice the one-arm cost; no dataset-specific tuning
alternatives.benefit: Tests both directions relative to stored alpha1 without fitting weights to the small gradient probe.

alternatives.recommendation: Do not use in this bounded experiment
alternatives.reason: Derived from selected checkpoints and three Train batches; introduces additional tuning and does not account for AdamW or the training trajectory.

launch_conditions: Source941/input/log1p/head/memory/model/budget/seed/rawRMSE selection remain unchanged; inherited baseline is never retrained or reevaluated.
Synthetic alpha1 run must match the prior training scalar, gradients, initial state/RNG, update and selection behavior; alpha is bound into checkpoint/resume identity and logs.
Do not renormalize alpha*time+quantity or replace with time+quantity/alpha: overall objective scaling interacts with global clipping, AdamW epsilon and weight decay.
Each new condition may retain the approved36h limit from its own start, but existing host absolute168h deadline and paused Cap27 deadlines must not reset or extend.

Before launching, exact paused process identity and stopped state form an allowed retained-GPU-context set. New3-worker native admission must fit actual remaining memory; no signals or resource reclamation from paused jobs.
Report all candidate/seed RMSE,MAE and TimeNLL tradeoffs; no winner-only reporting or causal/generalization claims.
interpretation: This tests joint-objective weighting, not a new backbone contribution or an optimal loss weight. Batch-gradient imbalance is a motivation, not an established causal mechanism.
